newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia port strike blocks coffee exports.
newsitem.headline: Colombia port strike blocks coffee exports.

text.p: A three-day-old strike by Colombia dock workers in the main Pacific coast port of Buenaventura has halted the export of "about" 160,000 60-kg bags of coffee, a top coffee official said Friday.

About 60 percent of all coffee exports are shipped out through Buenaventura. John Naranjo, commercial manager of the National Coffee Growers' Federation said the 160,000 bags were blocked in port either in trucks or already loaded on to containers.

An agreement in principle to end the strike was reached between cargo handling companies, or operators, and dock workers' representatives Thursday morning but workers rejected the deal in a general assembly Thursday evening.

"This situation is very worrying. We did our sums and realized that between the coffee on trucks and that already loaded into containers, all of which is blocked in port, there are 160,000 bags," Naranjo told Reuters.
"U.S. roasters are crying out for coffee because we understand their stocks are running low. But for the time being there is nothing we can do," he added.

Earlier in the week, the federation estimated 90,000 60-kg bags had been paralyzed by the industrial action. The regional El Pais newspaper reported Friday that Labor Ministry officials had gone to the port to try and resolve the dispute, which centers on workers demands for higher wages, sickness and injury benefits and changes in the way they are contracted.
